policy_title: Support self-ID for trans and non-binary people and end spousal veto
stated: Support self-ID for trans and non-binary people to be legally recognised in their chosen gender. End the spousal veto for married trans people to acquire gender recognition certificates and allow an X gender marker on passports.

source.quote: The Green Party supports self-ID, so that trans and non-binary people could be legally recognised in their chosen gender through self-declaration. We also support ending the spousal veto so that married trans people can acquire their gender recognition certification without having to obtain permission from their spouse, and to change the law so an X gender marker can be added to passports for non-binary and intersex people who wish to use it.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly reforms the legal framework for gender recognition (GRCs), removes a due-process barrier (spousal veto), and extends official identity documentation options — all squarely within O9's scope of legal/civil rights, equal treatment, due process, and treatment of a minority group.

Replacing medicalised gatekeeping (diagnostic requirements, Gender Recognition Panel approval) with self-declaration removes a specific form of state coercion over legal identity and bodily self-determination, concretely moving the 'freedom from state coercion / bodily autonomy' indicator.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O9 for the equal-treatment/legal-status effect on trans and non-binary people, and O10 for the removal of compulsory medical-state gatekeeping over personal identity. Other fundamentals (O5, O15) are frequently invoked in public debate but the causal chain from GRC reform to specific indicators (crime rates, social trust scores) is too contested and indirect to clear the non-negligible bar without routing through further contested steps.
